text.p: - Slovenian parliament on Thursday rejected the new cabinet proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek by an even vote of 45 against 45. Drnovsek has to present a new government line-up within 10 days.

- Slovenia will together with other successors of the former Yugoslavia continue its efforts to freeze former Yugoslavia's assets, estimated at $1.5 billion, said Miran Mejak, leader of Slovenia's group taking part in successor talks.
- Some 1,500 people on Thursday protested in front of parliament against the government line-up, claiming that the proposed government is illegal.
- In Slovenia there are still some 10,000 refugees from Bosnia.
- Car maker Revoz, partner of France's Renault, increased 1996 production by two percent and exports by five percent compared to 1995.

- Ironworks production rose 23 percent to 396,000 tonnes in 1996, with losses narrowing to 1.8 billion tolars ($12 million) from 5.7 billion tolars, while sales rose 30 percent to 67 billion tolars ($44.7 million).

- An opinion poll shows that 47.4 percent of Slovenians see the governemnt proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek as legitimate, while 26.2 thought it was not, with the remained undecided.
- Slovenia's industrial output in 1996 rose by one percent compared to the previous year, the statistical office reported.
- Smelt Olimpija lost 67-70 against Spain's Seville at Thursday's basketball game of the Euroleague group G.

- Construction company GPG decided to change the structure of its shares listed on the Ljubljana bourse due to changes in its privatisation process. The nominal value of its shares is now 10,000 tolars ($66.7).
